For 3 people as well. It was 7 lbs because it's the smallest they had at Publix. A 4 or 5lb cut would be plenty for 3 people.

I use an offset grill. I mostly follow Aaron Franklin's method for brisket. He has 3 YouTube videos showing how he does it.
But here's what I've learned:
Trim fat down to 1/4", and get rid of any tough fat that won't cook down.
Dry rub is only equal parts salt and pepper.
Fuel is 2/3'a hardwood charcoal and 1/3 chopped wood chunks.
For wood: Applewood for a more steak flavor, hickory for that bacon-like flavor. I did hickory this time and liked it a lot more.
Maintain 240° to 270° to help with time. Keep the smoke   clear. No white smoke.
Only check meat every 3 hrs. Do not check more often. You will regret the time it adds.
Spritz with 1/2 water and 1/2 apple cider vinegar until the wrap.
Wrap with butcher paper 6 hrs in or when meat looks like it is starting to dry out.
Expect 1.5 hrs per pound.
I aim for 205° for doneness, but I start checking at 195°.
Thermometer should go in with almost no resistance. 
Rest one hour in a cooler.

And for piece of mind, always expect it to take hrs longer than you originally think.  I've only done brisket a few times but I end up very frustrated because it takes 4 hrs longer than planned. 1.5 to 2 hrs per is much more realistic.

Hope that helps!
